explanation: `HasDirichletDensity` and `primeIdealZetaSum` are defined in Mathlib, in `Mathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/DirichletDensity.lean`, and no other Mathlib file mentions `DirichletDensity`. I read that whole file. It proves `primeIdealZetaSum_le_card_of_finite`, `hasDirichletDensity_empty`, and the `nonneg`/`le_one` bounds, but has no lemma saying that a finite set has Dirichlet density 0. Getting that result needs more than one Mathlib lemma. The library's helper `hasDirichletDensity_zero_of_eventually_le` (the partial sums stay bounded while the full sum tends to infinity) is not in Mathlib; it is combined here with Mathlib's `primeIdealZetaSum_le_card_of_finite`. This is more than a one- or two-line derivation, so it does not count as a special case.
